info.name: Workshop Management API
info.description:
The main flows of the workshop operation, in the order they happen.

## Before running

1. `docker compose up -d`
2. `npm run migration:run`
3. `npm run seed`

The seed creates one user per role plus the catalog, stock, customer and vehicle data this collection uses. Import the `workshop-api.local.postman_environment.json` environment as well.

## How to run it

Through the Collection Runner, top to bottom: each folder stores in a variable what the next one needs. The `00. Authentication` folder is required and comes first. The `07. Wrap-up` folder drops the sessions, so it goes last.

The requests that create accounts generate a valid CPF and a unique email on every run, because the database is not cleaned between them.

A full run consumes almost the whole authentication rate limit quota, so two runs back to back get a 429. Wait for the window to close, or raise the limit in `.env`.

item.name: 00. Authentication
item.description: Signs in as each actor `npm run seed` creates. Run this folder first: every other one uses the tokens it stores.

request.description: Full administrative access: users, roles, catalog, inventory and work orders.
Service advisor: receives the customer, opens the work order and builds the budget.
Mechanic: diagnoses, executes and completes the work order.
The seeded customer: follows and decides the budget of their own orders.
The only route that returns the user's own identifier alongside the roles and permissions. The work order needs it to assign the mechanic.

exec: pm.test('carries the effective roles and permissions', () => pm.expect(body.roles).to.include('MECHANIC'));

request.description: The refresh token is single use: the response carries a new pair and the old one stops working.

exec: pm.test('the current session is flagged', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().some((s) => s.current)).to.be.true);

item.name: 01. Customer onboarding
item.description: From the account to the first vehicle. The account is created on a public route, receives the CUSTOMER role, becomes a customer record and gains a vehicle.

request.description: The only write route with no authentication. It has a rate limit of its own, tighter than the global one.

exec: // A valid CPF and a unique email on every run: the test database is never truncated.
const digit = (ds, weight) => { const s = ds.reduce((t, d, i) => t + d * (weight - i), 0); const r = s % 11; return r < 2 ? 0 : 11 - r; };

request.description: Stores the CUSTOMER and MECHANIC identifiers, used here and in folder 02.
Idempotent. Without this role, the customer registration in the next step is refused.
Links the workshop record to the existing account. Address and phone are optional, but the address is all or nothing.
Accepts the old format (AAA0000) and the Mercosul one (AAA0A00), with or without separators.

exec: // A drawn Mercosul plate (AAA0A00): the plate is unique among active vehicles.

item.name: Sign in as the new customer

exec: pm.test('the phone number was normalised to digits', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().phoneNumber).to.eql('1932321010'));

item.name: 02. User management
item.description: Staff accounts and the access model. A staff account is born with a temporary password and only gets past the guards after the change.

exec: pm.test('the permission catalog is not empty', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json()).to.have.lengthOf.at.least(1));

request.description: The temporary password appears only in this response and is never written to a log. Until the change, the account reaches only /users/me/password.

exec: const digit = (ds, weight) => { const s = ds.reduce((t, d, i) => t + d * (weight - i), 0); const r = s % 11; return r < 2 ? 0 : 11 - r; };
pm.test('the temporary password comes exactly once', () => pm.expect(body.temporaryPassword).to.be.a('string'));

item.name: Assign the MECHANIC role to the staff account

request.description: roleMechanicId comes from the role listing in folder 01.
Returns the roles assigned directly to the user, each with its identifier and name.

exec: pm.test('the MECHANIC role shows up', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().roles.map((r) => r.name)).to.include('MECHANIC'));

item.name: Sign in as the staff account with the temporary password

request.description: Ends every session of the user, including the one that made the change. Signing in again is required afterwards.
Logical deletion: the row stays, the sessions drop and the account disappears from the listings.

item.name: 03. Inventory management
item.description: Parts and supplies with a truthful count. The quantity on hand is never written directly: only a movement changes it.

request.description: `kind` accepts PART or SUPPLY. The item is born with a quantity of zero.

exec: pm.test('is born with a quantity of zero', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().quantityOnHand).to.eql(0));

request.description: Send `description: null` to clear the description; omit the field to leave it untouched.

exec: pm.test('the quantity does not change on a PATCH', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().quantityOnHand).to.eql(0));

request.description: Writes an INBOUND movement and raises the count.
The reason is mandatory on an adjustment, unlike a replenishment. The count never goes negative.
Append-only ledger: no movement is edited or erased.
Items whose demand from orders in execution exceeds what is on the shelf.
Logical deletion. Refused with 409 while any work order that planned the item has not been delivered or cancelled. The count and the history stay, and the SKU becomes free again.

item.name: The deactivated item left the listing

exec: pm.test('no longer shows up in the active catalog', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().some((i) => i.id === pm.collectionVariables.get('newItemId'))).to.be.false);

item.name: 04. Work order management
item.description: The full flow, in the order the state machine accepts: RECEIVED, IN DIAGNOSIS, AWAITING APPROVAL, IN EXECUTION, COMPLETED, DELIVERED.

request.description: The counter starts from the CPF or CNPJ. The identifier found here is what opens the work order.
Born in RECEIVED. A vehicle can have only one open work order at a time.

exec: pm.test('is born with a number of its own', () => pm.expect(body.number).to.be.a('string'));

request.description: The status changes on its own, as a consequence of the action. There is no route to write a status by hand.

exec: pm.test('the mechanic is recorded on the order', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().assignedMechanicUserId).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('mechanicUserId')));

request.description: The price comes from the catalog. No route accepts a price from the caller.

exec: pm.test('the order now carries a service', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().serviceItems).to.have.lengthOf.at.least(1));

request.description: Planning moves no stock. The write-down happens at withdrawal, further along.

exec: pm.test('the part enters planned, without leaving the shelf', () => pm.expect(part.withdrawnQuantity).to.eql(0));

item.name: Complete the diagnosis and generate the budget

request.description: The budget is summed inside the aggregate, from the services and the planned parts. The total comes from no input field.

exec: pm.test('round 1 was generated with a total', () => pm.expect(body.budgets[0].totalCents).to.be.above(0));

request.description: The decision belongs to the order's owner or to whoever holds work-orders:decide. A stranger gets a 404, not a 403: someone else's number does not exist for them.
Decreases the stock, writes the movement and updates the order in a single transaction.

exec: pm.test('the part leaves the shelf and enters the order', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().partItems[0].withdrawnQuantity).to.eql(2));

request.description: Charges what was withdrawn, at the budgeted price. A part planned and never withdrawn does not enter the bill.
The reason is mandatory and the discount cannot exceed the charged total.

exec: pm.test('the discount is recorded with its reason', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().discountCents).to.eql(1000));

request.description: Closes the book: the pending stock consumptions become settled.

exec: pm.test('the delivered order shows up on the board', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().some((o) => o.number === pm.collectionVariables.get('workOrderNumber'))).to.be.true);

request.description: The vehicle is free again: the previous order was delivered.
Cancelling in execution requires a permission of its own and writes off the parts already withdrawn.

item.name: 05. Customer tracking
item.description: What the customer sees of their own orders. None of these routes accepts someone else's identifier.

item.name: One of my orders, by number

exec: pm.test('carries the budget and the status', () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.status).to.eql('DELIVERED'); pm.expect(b.budgets).to.have.lengthOf.at.least(1); });

request.description: The same answer as a non-existent number. There is no way to discover someone else's order from a difference in the error.

exec: pm.test('someone else number does not exist for the caller', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().code).to.eql('WORK_ORDER_NOT_FOUND'));

item.name: 06. Metrics and audit
item.description: What the operation measures and what stays on record.

request.description: Accepts the serviceId, completedFrom and completedTo filters. With a service filter the response is marked as approximated: an order carrying several services contributes its whole elapsed time to each one.

exec: pm.test('returns the average and the count', () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b).to.have.property('workOrderCount'); });
pm.test('the response is marked as approximated', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().approximated).to.be.true);

request.description: Written inside the same transaction that changes the aggregate: there is no step applied without a record.

exec: pm.test('records each step in chronological order', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json()).to.have.lengthOf.at.least(5));

item.name: 07. Wrap-up
item.description: Leave this for last: signing out drops every active session of the user, not only the current one.

exec: pm.test('reports how many sessions were dropped', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().revokedSessions).to.be.at.least(1));
